summary.title: Write You A Scheme, Version 2
summary.one_liner: A chapter-by-chapter table of contents for building a Scheme interpreter in Haskell, covering parsing, evaluation, errors, primitives, REPL, IO, standard library, and testing.
keywords: how to write a scheme interpreter
takeaways: The series builds a Scheme interpreter in Haskell in stages.
Parsing turns program text into an abstract syntax tree.
Evaluation interprets the AST using monad transformers.
Later chapters add error handling, a primitive environment, a REPL, file IO, a standard library, and tests.
summary.summary: This page is the table of contents for the Write You a Scheme, Version 2 series by Adam Wespiser. It lists chapters covering the overall design, Scheme syntax and semantics in Haskell, parsing text into an abstract syntax tree, evaluation with monad transformers, error checking and exceptions, primitive functions, a read-eval-print loop, input/output, a standard library built from primitives, and tests. The page itself contains only chapter titles and short descriptions, so the actual implementation details are in the linked chapters, which were not read.
